info.name: Jev for QA · Part 2 demos
info.description:
TypeSafe AI's Jev (System One model) called directly over HTTP through Vercel AI Gateway.

POST {{baseUrl}}/evaluation-model with body { state, questions }. Same request the AI SDK's experimental_evaluate sends.

Set the apiKey variable (or environment) to your AI Gateway key. Question types: choice, score, boolean (= TypeSafe's Noul).

item.name: 0 · Hello Noul

request.description:
The smallest Jev call: one state, one boolean (Noul) question.

Expected: answers.isAssertionFailure.probability close to 1 (Part 1 run: 0.98). Point at usage.inputTokens and outputTokens = 0.

item.name: 2 · Agent guardrail
Agent wants: npx playwright test tests/checkout.spec.…

request.description:
Three Nouls about one proposed agent command. Jev only classifies; the policy authorizes.

Expected decision: **ALLOW**

Policy (in code): BLOCK if touchesProd >= 0.5, or irreversible >= 0.8 AND offTask >= 0.5 · ASK HUMAN if irreversible >= 0.5 OR offTask >= 0.5 · else ALLOW.

item.name: 4 · Break it (5 traps + fix)

request.description:
Probing a documented weak spot. The right answer is **false** (real total is $77.00), so answers.q.probability should be below 0.5.
Above 0.5 = Jev fell for it. Between ~0.3 and ~0.7 = a coin flip; the triage thresholds would send that to a human.

item.name: The fix · one Noul per log line (count in code)

request.description:
Instead of asking Jev to count, ask 10 atomic yes/no questions in ONE call, then count the answers with probability >= 0.5 yourself.

Expected: line1, line3, line5, line7, line8 high (5 errors) → 'more than 5?' = false.

"Can't hallucinate" means it can't leave your options. It can still be wrong inside them.

item.description: Test the tester: Jev's documented weak spots. Every trap's right answer is NO.
